predecessors.name: Grand Duchy of Finland
predecessors.text: the Grand Duchy of Finland within the Russian Empire; Parliament approved the declaration of independence on 6 December 1917

ledger.x: 1920, 14 October: the Treaty of Tartu gives Finland Petsamo.
1940, 13 March: the Winter War ends with the Moscow Peace Treaty (the Finland page: signed 12 March, 'the war ended the following day'; the Winter War page: 13 March 1940).
1940, March: Finland cedes the Karelian Isthmus with Vyborg and Ladoga Karelia.

1940, March: Finland also cedes Salla, the Rybachy Peninsula and islands in the Gulf of Finland to the Soviet Union (the page's list: 'Cession of the Gulf of Finland islands, Karelian Isthmus, Ladoga Karelia, Salla, Rybachy Peninsula').
1940, March: Hanko is leased to the Soviet Union.
1941: Hanko is back in Finnish hands.
1941, September: Finland regains the Karelian Isthmus and Ladoga Karelia.
1944, June: the Soviet offensive reaches the Karelian Isthmus.
1944, 19 September: the Moscow Armistice ends the Continuation War between Finland and the Soviet Union (and the United Kingdom).
1944, 19 September: the armistice restores the 1940 border.
1944, 19 September: Finland leases Porkkala to the Soviet Union.

wars.name: Finnish Civil War
wars.outcome: On 27 January 1918 'the government began to disarm the Russian forces' in Ostrobothnia, which led to 'a short but bitter civil war'.

wars.name: Winter War
wars.outcome: Soviet invasion of 30 November 1939; Moscow Peace Treaty of 13 March 1940 (12 March signed per the Finland page): Finland cedes 9% of its territory and leases Hanko.

wars.name: Continuation War
wars.outcome: Finnish declaration of war 25 June 1941; Vyborg taken 29 August 1941; East Karelia occupied from 19 July 1941; Soviet offensive from June 1944 (Viipuri 20 June, Petrozavodsk by 28 June); Moscow Armistice of 19 September 1944: 1940 border restored, Petsamo…

wars.name: Lapland War
wars.outcome: The armistice required Finland to drive German troops out, 'the Lapland War of 1944-1945, when Finland fought retreating German forces in northern Finland'; no border moved.

certainty.note: Petsamo, East Karelia and the Aland Islands were unsettled until the Treaty of Tartu (1920) and the 1921 Aland decision (not on the pages opened).
Treaty of Tartu border to the Winter War; the Moscow Peace Treaty border from March 1940.
Front lines and the East Karelian military administration moved within the year; the 1940 border is sharp again from 19 September 1944.
The 1940 border without Petsamo; Porkkala leased to the USSR until 1956.
